title: Epochal credit persistency gap during policy shadow-deployment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: We observed intermittent customer-facing quota throttles and billing anomalies that correlate with policy shadow-deploys and epoch boundary handoffs. Affected paths: per-key and per-route allowance accounting when the policy-engine applies a hierarchical merge (org -> route -> key) during shadow rollout. The symptom is a transient reversion of credit state that allows short bursts or incorrectly attributes usage to the wrong window, producing both silent over-allow (missed throttles) and double-billing in downstream aggregates.

Sightings:
- First reported by SRE from spike alerts on 2026-03-08 (high SLO error budget burn, spike in "unmetered_usage" events).
- Internal test harness (replay of customer traffic) reproduced a ~30-90s window where token counters for keys briefly revert to an earlier epoch snapshot when policy-shadow merges occur.
- Billing pipelines show duplicated delta records for some keys across epoch boundaries during the same minute.

Reproduction steps:
1) Deploy a policy change as a shadow for a set of routes with hierarchical exemptions (org-level override + route-level specific limits).
2) Simulate high-concurrency traffic for a target org+route+key mixture using the region-edge staging fleet.
3) Force an epoch roll (fast-forward simulated clock) while the shadow policy is transitioning to active for a subset of shards.
4) Observe per-key allowance metrics: counter resets, duplicate debits, and a short window of silent-allow for repeated requests.

Hypothesis:
- During a shadow-to-active promotion we apply a merge algorithm that snapshots per-key allowance state from multiple sources (existing shard in-memory, rendezvous from policy-store, and in-flight debit logs). The merge currently favors the oldest non-null snapshot but fails to monotonicize epoch offsets. When the chosen snapshot has an older epoch pointer, subsequent debits are applied on top of stale metadata and then reconciled, producing duplicated consumption records and transient negative deltas in aggregators.

Evidence:
- Trace excerpts attached in logs: request traces show policy-eval timestamps that step backward by ~60s relative to real time when the merge picks a stale shard snapshot.
- Redis shard dump from staging shows two conflicting per-key entries (v1: epoch=2026-03-08T14:02:00Z, credits=42; v2: epoch=2026-03-08T14:03:00Z, credits=10). After the merge, the runtime applied debits against epoch=14:02 which produced an extra 32 tokens of apparent usage.
- Billing event stream contains out-of-order sequence numbers for the affected key for the minute.

Immediate mitigations applied: 
- Rolled back the in-progress shadow deployments and paused automatic shadow promotions.
- Triage patch: added a defensive check in the merge path to enforce epoch monotonicity (if incoming snapshot.epoch < local.epoch then prefer local and emit a reconcile-warning metric). Deployed to staging and saw the reproduction window shrink but not fully eliminated.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strict monotonic preference prevents some legitimate recovery merges after shard failover; we need a safe tie-breaker that is both monotonic and allows correct reconciliation in failover cases.
- Whether to move reconciliation logic out of the hot path (async background reconcile) to avoid impacting latency.

Next steps (plan):
- Deep-dive pairing session (Dan + Asha) to instrument all merge code paths with epoch provenance tags and increased sampling for affected routes (ETA 2026-03-13).
- Implement and test a deterministic merge policy: (1) choose snapshot with max(epoch, last-applied-seq), (2) if stale snapshot must be applied, convert debits to idempotent reconciliation entries rather than direct counter writes. (estimate: 3 points, PR + canary).
- Add a reconciliation consumer that detects duplicate debits in billing stream and emits compensating zero-sum events for auditors (low-latency fix for billing accuracy).
- Postmortem and customer communications: prepare explainer and remediation steps for affected customers; include audit of billing backfill needs.

Relevant artifacts / links: 
- Staging trace logs: https://redwood-internal/traces/trace-2026-03-08-epoch-merge
- Reproduction harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-sim/tree/ephemeral-merge-tests
- Temporary triage PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/1294

Owners & reviewers: 
- Primary: Daniel Kim (assignee)
- Secondary: Asha Patel (creator), Luis Ortega (runtime), Minh Tran (billing)

Acceptance criteria: 
- Deterministic merge algorithm implemented and unit-tested to guarantee no epoch regression possibility in normal promotion path.
- Staging replay shows zero duplicated debit records in the minute window for the previously affected keys.
- Billing pipeline either shows no double-charge or a compensating backfill plan is executed and verified.

If blocked: escalate to runtime oncall and billing team for a coordinated rollback of recent policy-store schema changes.
